text:
Maya: Quick design call  should the onboarding samples be a dismissible modal or a pinned strip (pinned strip = top-of-console, subtle)? Im leaning pinned strip to avoid interrupting flows.
Owen: Pinned strip. Modals block keyboard nav and feel like a roadblock.
Priya: Research backs that — users dismiss modals. A shallow "pinned strip" with 3 starters increased completion in our study.
Jon: Dev impact: strip needs responsive behavior for narrow screens. Estimate 2 dev days for core + 1 for responsive tweaks. Modal is quicker but needs a11y patchwork.
Maya: Accessibility: strip must be reachable via skip-link, announce on first visit only, and not trap focus when expanded. Priya, can you add a checklist?
Priya: Yep. Checklist: skip-link, aria-live first-render, keyboard collapse/expand, contrast on labels. I'll attach to PR.
Owen: Copy proposal: header = "Try a starter project" subtitle = "3 quick demos to get Redwood running" microcopy CTA = "Start sample"
Maya: Sounds good. Also lets wire samples into the onboarding checklist so completing one marks a step done. Use query param linking like /org/123?sample=vector to keep it stateless.
Jon: Agreed. Example link: <Link to={`/org/${orgId}?sample=${slug}`}>Launch</Link>
onboard-bot: Heads up: attach Figma handoff and tokens by Friday.
Maya: Decision: implement pinned strip MVP (compact chips), route-param linking, analytics events (strip_shown, sample_started, strip_collapsed). Follow-up: full thumbnail carousel A/B test.
Priya: I'll run keyboard/a11y checks on the PR.
Owen: Starting branch today, will flag PR when ready.
Maya: Thanks all  moving to sprint board. :rocket:
